HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

Patient: John Doe DOB: 21 Dec 1986 Encounter: Video consult with Dr. Jacob  
Date: [today’s date not documented]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
History:
• Chief complaint: Severe, persistent headache x 4 days.  
• Course/associated features:
  – Headache began first; subjective fever followed (“feel hot,” no recorded temperature).  
  – Generalized myalgias; feels cold but no rigors/shivering.  
  – Diffuse red, itchy rash over entire body; blanching on glass test.  
  – Denies photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting, pins/needles, focal weakness, cough, coryza, ear pain.  
• Recent travel: Returned from Thailand ≈1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travelling companion also unwell.  
• Medications tried for symptom relief: Paracetamol and ibuprofen (ineffective).  

Past Medical History:
• Chronic medical conditions: None reported.  
• Surgical history: None reported.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other regular medicines.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social / other: No details on smoking, alcohol, occupation provided.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-consult; no hands-on exam performed)
• General: Alert, conversant via video.  
• Rash: Patient-reported diffuse red, itchy, blanching rash.  
• Neurological: No reported focal deficits; denies photophobia and neck stiffness.  
• No further vitals or system examinations documented.

Impression:
Acute febrile illness with severe headache and blanching generalized rash following recent travel to Thailand – possible viral infection (e.g., dengue or other arbovirus) vs early meningitis; needs urgent in-person evaluation.

Management Plan:
• Advised urgent face-to-face assessment in Babylon hub/GP clinic within the next few hours.  
• Warned possibility of hospital referral for further evaluation (incl. blood tests).  
• If no immediate appointment available, attend Emergency Department.  
• Continue symptomatic relief with paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed.  
• Safety-net: Seek emergency care if headache worsens, new neurological symptoms, non-blanching rash, persistent high fever, or vomiting develop.

Patient Summary:
Mr. Doe presents with a 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, and a blanching itchy rash after recent travel to Thailand. Viral illness (including dengue) or early meningitis considered. He has been directed to obtain urgent in-person assessment and possible further investigations today.

Key Takeaways:
1. Attend an urgent GP/hub appointment today; go directly to ED if not available.  
2. Continue paracetamol/ibuprofen for comfort; monitor for worsening or new red-flag symptoms.  
3. Expect possible blood tests and hospital review depending on in-person findings.

Next Steps:
• Same-day GP/hub visit for full physical exam and vitals.  
• Likely labs: CBC, liver function, malaria/dengue screening, blood cultures as indicated.  
• Consider lumbar puncture if meningitis suspected following exam.  
• Arrange follow-up or ED referral based on initial in-person assessment results.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Quality checks:

Missing/expected elements:
• No documented vital signs (temperature, BP, HR, RR).  
• No ophthalmologic, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal exams performed/recorded.  
• No social history (smoking/alcohol), immunization status, or family history obtained.

Internal conflicts:
• None noted (photophobia and neck stiffness consistently denied).

Transcript quality:
• Clear; occasional conversational fillers but overall information understandable.
